newsitem.title: USA: Cincinnati Gas gains leeway to issue debt.
newsitem.headline: Cincinnati Gas gains leeway to issue debt.

text.p: Shareholders of The Cincinnati Gas & Electric Co voted to remove a provision limiting the company's ability to issue unsecured debt, including short-term paper.
CINergy Corp, the parent holding company and sole holder of the company's common stock, and holders of preferred stock voted at a special meeting to remove the provision, CINergy said Wednesday.
It said the company would make a special cash payment of $1 per share to each preferred stockholder who voted in favor of the amendment.
CINergy also said it bought about 85 percent of the company's 2.0 million preferred shares after making a tender offer. It said the offer was conditioned upon the approval of the amendment.
In August, CINergy said it would pay $64 a share for the four percent series preferred stock, $80 for the 4-3/4 percent series, $116 for the 7-7/8 percent series and $110 for the 7-3/8 series.
It added that the company only made the special cash payment to those preferred shareholders who had not sold their stake to CINergy.
